references.title: S. V. Konyagin, Estimates of the least prime factor of a binomial coefficient, Mathematika 46 (1999) 41-55
references.note: g(k) >= exp(c (log k)^2) for large k, where g(k) is the least n > k+1 with C(n,k) having no prime factor <= k

references.title: A. Granville and O. Ramaré, Explicit bounds on exponential sums and the scarcity of squarefree binomial coefficients, Mathematika 43 (1996) 73-107
references.note: earlier bound g(k) >= exp(c sqrt(log^3 k / log log k)), also enough

references.title: Annex 301ade26 on erdos-1094--h2 (the split this node came from)

summary: Follows from a published bound, not formalised. For n >= k^2 an exception has no prime factor <= k, so C(n,k) is good and n >= g(k). Konyagin's g(k) >= exp(c (log k)^2) exceeds k^3 once log k > 3/c, so for all large k there is no exception with n < k^3, and K can be taken as the last k below that point. The constant c is not explicit in what I read, so a formal proof needs an explicit lower bound for g(k).
